newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich flotation set for July.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich flotation set for July.

text.p: Britain's Woolwich Building Society said on Monday that qualifying customers would receive 450 free shares upon its conversion to a public company later this year.
The building society, the third largest in the UK, with assets of more than 30 billion pounds, said it expects flotation to take place in July.
The Woolwich said it expected basic distribution of 450 free shares to some 2.57 million persons, which include qualifying employees and qualifying pensioners.

It said the average distribution to members, including the variable element, would be 1,233 pounds ($2,090), although the exact distribution would depend on the size of members' balances at relevant qualifying dates. An additional handout of up to 2,000 free shares will be made to savers who have been with the society for more than two years.

The building society has not yet announced its flotation price but its financial advisors came with an historic valuation that gives its market capitalisation would have been between 2.96 and 3.38 billion pounds with a mid value of 3.17 billion had the conversion occurred and Woolwich been listed on the London Stock Exchange on 20 December. This represents a range of price per share of between 175 pence and 200 pence with a mid price of 187.5 pence.

John Stewart, Woolwich chief Executive, said, "I urge all members to support our conversion plans. Following flotation, we expect Woolwich Plc to be one of the top ten UK banks in terms of total asset size and to be included in the FT-SE 100 Index."
A special general meeting will be held on February 10 to vote on the proposals. ($1=.5899 Pound)
